paragraphs.text: On 09/06/2026 Tom Ellis, physiotherapist, recorded an assessment of acute non-specific mechanical low back pain following a lifting injury at work on 02/06/2026, with no red flags and no neurological signs. On 22/09/2026 Tom Ellis recorded the assessment as mechanical low back pain following the workplace lifting injury on 02/06/2026.

[CLAIMANT] reported that on 02/06/2026, during a night shift, he lifted a carton of approximately 20 kg from floor level onto a pallet, twisting to the right, with immediate sharp pain across the low back, right more than left.

Tom Ellis, physiotherapist, recorded treatment of soft tissue mobilisation to the right lumbar paraspinals and quadratus lumborum, Maitland grade II central posteroanterior glides at L4–L5 and heat on 09/06/2026. On 16/06/2026 he recorded grade III central glides at L4–L5 and right unilateral posteroanterior glides at L4/5, and on 30/06/2026 soft tissue mobilisation and grade III central glides at L4–L5. He recorded reassurance and advice to stay active on 09/06/2026, advice on pacing for the return to amended duties on 16/06/2026, and a discussion of manual handling technique (hip hinge, load close to the body, turning the feet rather than twisting) on 30/06/2026.

A home exercise programme was set on 09/06/2026 (pelvic tilts, knee rolls, cat–camel, walking 20 min/day building up) and progressed on 16/06/2026 (bridges, bird-dog, sit-to-stand) and 30/06/2026 (hip hinge with dowel, bodyweight goblet squat, side plank). On 14/07/2026 Sarah Reid, senior physiotherapist, recorded education on graded loading and load tolerance, progression to loaded strength work (kettlebell deadlift 12 kg, goblet squat 8 kg, side plank) and sessions reduced to every 3–4 weeks alongside a self-directed gym programme. On 11/08/2026 Tom Ellis recorded a review of gym exercise technique and progression of the programme (kettlebell deadlift 16 kg, suitcase carry, step-ups). On 22/09/2026 he recorded discharge to self-management, with advice to continue the gym programme 2–3 times a week and maintenance home exercises, and to contact the clinic if symptoms recur.
6 of 7 appointments were attended, with 0 did not attend and 1 late cancellation on 23/06/2026.
On 22/09/2026 Tom Ellis, physiotherapist, recorded that [CLAIMANT] was discharged from active physiotherapy to self-management.

On 22/09/2026 Tom Ellis, physiotherapist, recorded that [CLAIMANT] was on amended duties with occasional lifts up to 15 kg and no repetitive floor-level lifting. [CLAIMANT] reported low back pain of 1–2/10 at worst after 4 nights of shifts, settling on rest days, with no leg symptoms and no flare-ups in the last 6 weeks.

On 22/09/2026 Tom Ellis recorded that lumbar active range of movement was full and pain-free in all directions, and an Oswestry Disability Index score of 18%, assessed as minimal disability. He recorded that, in his opinion, [CLAIMANT] should avoid repetitive lifting more than 15 kg for 4 weeks.

On 22/09/2026 Tom Ellis, physiotherapist, recorded that in his opinion [CLAIMANT] is fit for a phased return to normal duties over 2 weeks, should avoid repetitive lifting more than 15 kg for 4 weeks, with review in 6 weeks. He recorded the same as a return-to-work recommendation for HR and occupational health.
